items.title: Hierarchical Fast--Slow ReAct Agent for Zero-Shot Object-Goal Navigation
items.abstract: Zero-shot object-goal navigation (ZSON) requires a robot to find a named object category in a building it has never entered. The prevailing approach scores frontiers with a vision--language \emph{value map}: every decision is another argmax over the map as it currently stands, and the evidence behind that score is discarded the moment it is taken. Systems that place a large vision--language model inside the perception--action loop typically query it on a fixed schedule from the current view alone; a room the robot walked through minutes earlier is never reconsidered, and a failed call has no defined fallback. We turn what the robot has already seen into the object of deliberation. Our hierarchical fast--slow agent leaves the value-map controller running at every step and writes a \emph{coordinate-anchored memory} as it moves: a semantic grid of room types and confirmed object instances, together with a bounded store of pose-tagged keyframes. A VLM screens each candidate detection before it is written. A deliberative layer reads this memory in a bounded reason--retrieve--act loop. It wakes on structural events the reactive layer computes, reasons first over text, and recalls a first-person view only for candidates that text alone cannot separate. Per-invocation and per-run caps bound its calls, a call-free first tier resolves the most frequent stall, and any failure returns control to the reactive controller. Our system reaches 68.75% SR on HM3D v1 \texttt{val} and 47.29% on MP3D \texttt{val}, the highest success rate among the zero-shot methods compared here. Choosing among far frontiers by argmax instead of deliberating costs 3.40 SR points in a paired comparison over all 2000 HM3D episodes (95\% CI [1.70, 5.05]); deliberating over every frontier does not recover them.

items.llm_tldr_en: Proposes a hierarchical fast-slow ReAct agent that deliberates over past observations to improve zero-shot object-goal navigation, leaving the value-map controller as the fast loop.
items.llm_tldr_cn: 现有零样本目标导航系统每次决策只看当前价值地图，丢弃历史证据，而大视觉语言模型按固定频率查询当前视角，无法重新审视已走过的房间。本文提出分层快慢ReAct智能体，将机器人已见内容作为思考对象，由价值地图控制器作为快循环，由慢循环对大模型进行调度与回退。该方法在未见过的建筑中实现了更好的目标搜索能力。

items.title: Rethink Before You Execute: Adaptive Execution for World Action Models
items.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) jointly predict future actions and the evolution of the environment. At each inference, a WAM generates a chunk of actions and the robot executes a fixed prefix before replanning. We argue that this fixed execution horizon is poorly matched to execution dynamics: the chunk reliability varies across task stages, so when to replan depends on the result of accumulated execution, not on the step counts. We propose TempoWAM (Timing Execution by Monitoring Progress Online), a lightweight plug-and-play execution scheme for WAMs. A Recurrent Progress Monitor first estimates task progress from the current observation, task instruction, remaining actions, and execution history; and an Adaptive Execution Protocol then evaluates whether the chunk is advancing the task to decide if replanning is needed. To bridge the training-deployment gap, the protocol is calibrated by a task-dependent calibration factor with online adaptation. Experiments on LIBERO, RoboTwin, and real-world tasks show that TempoWAM consistently improves the efficiency-success trade-off of WAM execution. On real robots, it reduces WAM inferences by 26.9% on easy tasks while maintaining success, and improves success by 13.3 points on difficult tasks.

items.llm_tldr_en: Proposes TempoWAM, a plug-and-play execution scheme for world action models that monitors task progress online and adaptively decides when to replan, addressing the mismatch of fixed execution horizons.
items.llm_tldr_cn: 针对世界动作模型固定执行前缀与真实执行动态不匹配的问题，提出TempoWAM轻量级执行方案。它利用循环进度监测器从观测、指令、剩余动作和执行历史中估计任务进度，并由自适应执行协议决定重新规划时机。实验表明该方法能提升任务执行效率与鲁棒性，且即插即用。这项工作为世界模型在机器人控制中的在线决策执行提供了新思路。
